sentences.text:
Satosh Bhadoriya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 30
August, 2019
Author: Vishal Mishra

Bench: Vishal Mishra
 1
 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 M.Cr.C. No.35814/2019
 (Santosh Bhadoriya vs. State of M.P.)
Gwalior, Dated : 30.08.2019
 Shri Prashant Sharma with Shri Harshad Bahirani, counsel for the
applicant.
 Shri Aditya Singh Ghuraiya, Public Prosecutor for the
respondent
/ State

. 
Learned counsel for the rival parties are heard.
Case Diary is perused.
The applicant has filed this first application under section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of bail.

The applicant has been arrested by Police Station STF Bhopal, Wing Gwalior in connection with Crime No.12/2019 registered in relation to the offences punishable under sections 420, 272, 273 and 120-B of IPC and 51, 59 of Food Safety & Standard Act, 2006.

entities.text: Police Station STF Bhopal, Wing Gwalior
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is alleged by the counsel for the applicant that FIR has been registered for the aforesaid offences under IPC whereas the case in hand relates to Food Safety and Standards Act and should have been governed by the provisions of Food Safety Act.
The Sections of IPC are wrongly made applicable to the case of the applicant and they are not made out in the facts and circumstances of the case.
It is submitted that offence under section 420 of IPC has been registered against the applicant.

From the bare perusal of reading of Section 420 as well as 415 of IPC, it is apparently clear that in the facts and circumstances of the present case the aforesaid Sections are not attracted for the reason that there is no person who has made any complaint against the applicant regarding cheating and until and unless the basic requirement of Sections 415 and THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Santosh Bhadoriya vs. State of M.P.) 420 of IPC are completed, no offence is made out against the applicant under the aforesaid Sections.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Santosh Bhadoriya vs. State of M.P.) 420
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He has drawn attention of this Court to other Sections 272 and 273 of IPC and has argued that when specific Act is being provided with specific sections which has not been taken into consideration by the authorities and has registered the case under the Indian Penal Code.
The act of the present applicant if taken to be correct then also the provisions of Food Safety Act are applicable in the case and not that of IPC.

Thus, he has argued that Sections 272 Satosh Bhadoriya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 30 August, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139244496/
1 and 273 read with Section 120 of IPC are wrongly being made applicable to the case of the applicant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further alleged that from the bare reading of the FIR it is seen that, the FIR has been registered with respect to four places and with respect to the present applicant place No.2 Proprietor Firm Girraj Foods, Bheekampura Road, Lahar, District Bhind, the samples of milk were collected and with respect to the other three places the present applicant is having no relevance.

Thus, even under the Food Safety Act the offence is not made out as the procedure which has been adopted by the authorities of STF is not the proper procedure and the authorities being incompetent authorities to Act under the Food Safety Act.
The aforesaid procedure is to be done by the officer authorized as per act.
He has further argued that even if the offences are taken to be proved against the present applicant except 420 then also there is only an imprisonment of six months.
There is no criminal history against the present applicant, therefore, he has prayed for grant of bail.

Counsel for the applicant has relied upon the order passed by this Hon'ble Court in the case of Banshilal Agrawal vs. State of M.P. and THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Santosh Bhadoriya vs. State of M.P.) another, reported in 2010 (1) EFR 519.

entities.text: Banshilal Agrawal vs. State of M.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Santosh Bhadoriya vs. State of M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Per contra, the learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the bail application and has submitted that the investigation is pending consideration, therefore till the investigation is completed the applicant is not entitled for grant of bail rather he should be directed to cooperate with the investigation as the offences which have been registered are not the offences against the particular person, the aforesaid offences are offences against the society at large by the act of the present applicant dealing into manufacturing in sale of adulterated food products which are dangerous for human consumption and could have resulted fatal for a person consuming the same.

He has further submitted that several articles have been seized from the custody of the present applicant and his premises,
therefore, until the investigation is completed, he should not be granted bail.

It is further contended that the offences under IPC have rightly been registered against the present applicant as the offences under Sections 51 and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 were also registered along with.

It is further submitted that the proceedings are being carried out by the STF which is duly being constituted under the instructions of Superintendent of Police, STF Gwalior comprising of three persons out of which one is from the STF Police Department and two others were from the Food Safety Department.
Thus, the proceedings are being carried out by the authorized persons.
Accordingly, he has prayed for rejection of the application.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the case THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Santosh Bhadoriya vs. State of M.P.) diary.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Santosh Bhadoriya vs. State of M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: An STF has been constituted under the instructions of Superintendent of STF Gwalior and comprising of a person from the STF Police Department and the two others from the Food Safety Department.
The inquiry is pending consideration in the matter and the alleged offences which have been committed by the applicant are offences at large against the society.

The applicant is involved in manufacture and sale of adulterated food materials which are dangerous and harmful for human consumption because the same results to various uncurable diseases which ultimately results into deaths.
Thus, in the opinion of this Court until the investigation is completed in the matter no bail should be granted to the applicant.

Accordingly, finding no merits in the application the same is Satosh Bhadoriya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 30 August, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139244496/
2 hereby rejected at this stage with a liberty to the applicant to repeat after completion of the investigation.
